strings.name: Sylvia Earle
strings.summary: Earle began with algae research and combined diving, deep-sea technology and marine ecology. She led an all-women aquanaut team in 1970, walked on the seabed at about 381 metres in a diving suit in 1979, and later became NOAA chief scientist. She developed exploration equipment and founded Mission Blue, promoting ocean “Hope Spots” and connecting science with the public through books and film. strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Conducted marine research and deep-sea exploration, advancing ocean conservation, ecological awareness and public science communication.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Gibbstown, New Jersey, United States; born August 30, 1935.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Underwater research and exploration
strings.highlights.h1.text: Combined marine surveys, saturation diving and deep-sea suit experiments to expand underwater research methods.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Florida State degree (1955); Duke master’s (1956) and PhD (1966).
strings.highlights.h2.title: Hope Spots initiative
strings.highlights.h2.text: Through Mission Blue, mobilized scientists, communities and governments around important ocean areas and their conservation.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Mission Blue documentary
strings.timeline.t1.text: The film presented her exploration and conservation advocacy to a wider public.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Founded Mission Blue
strings.timeline.t2.text: Presented her global ocean Hope Spots vision at TED and developed a conservation action network.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Founded deep-sea technology company
strings.timeline.t3.text: Established Deep Ocean Exploration and Research to develop underwater exploration equipment.
strings.timeline.t4.title: NOAA chief scientist
strings.timeline.t4.text: Became the agency’s first woman chief scientist, serving until 1992.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Deep-sea walk
strings.timeline.t5.text: Walked on the seabed at about 1,250 feet in a JIM suit, distinct from later submersible descents.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Led women aquanauts
strings.timeline.t6.text: Led an all-women Tektite II team living and conducting research underwater.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Doctoral research completed
strings.timeline.t7.text: Completed Duke doctoral research concerning marine plants.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Undergraduate studies completed
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned her Florida State degree before further research at Duke.
